source_citation: 2024 review, The Fabaceae in Northeastern Mexico: Caesalpinioideae excluding Mimoseae, Cercidoideae and Detarioideae (Plants 13(17):2477); name checked against Kew POWO

morphology_source_reported.flowers: Petals 8.5–10 mm long; anthers constricted immediately below terminal symmetrical pore
morphology_source_reported.diagnostic_note: Identification key distinguishes from nearby taxa using persistent sepals and anther/ovule characters
morphology_source_reported.stems: Pubescent with simple retrorse hairs, gland-like hairs, and stiff setae
morphology_source_reported.leaflets: One pair per leaf; 1.3–1.8 times as long as wide
morphology_source_reported.petiolar_gland: Gland at insertion of leaflet pair
morphology_source_reported.sepals: Persist as immature fruit develops, contrasted with deciduous sepals of S. durangensis
morphology_source_reported.anthers: Constricted immediately below a symmetric terminal pollen pore
morphology_source_reported.fruit: Erect, with hairs and stiff bristles, persists after dehiscence; 2–4 cm long; published width 0.5–8 cm likely transcription/unit issue, withheld

habitat_source_reported: Desert scrubland 600–1450 m in northeastern Mexico region (not a Texas county habitat assessment)
